name: RAZOR
question: Is robot-assisted radical cystectomy with extracorporeal urinary diversion noninferior to open radical cystectomy for two-year progression-free survival in patients with bladder cancer?

arms.label: Robot-assisted radical cystectomy with extracorporeal urinary diversion
open radical cystectomy with extracorporeal urinary diversion

design.population: Adults with biopsy-proven clinical T1–T4, N0–N1, M0 bladder cancer or refractory carcinoma in situ eligible for radical cystectomy.
design.description: Multicenter, open-label phase 3 noninferiority randomized trial
design.locator: Lancet PDF pp2525,2527–2528, Methods and Figure 1

verdictNote: Two-year progression-free survival met the prespecified 15-percentage-point noninferiority margin.
takeaway: RAZOR compared robot-assisted with open radical cystectomy, both with extracorporeal urinary diversion. In the per-protocol population, robotic surgery met the prespecified noninferiority criterion for two-year progression-free survival (72.3% versus 71.6%; difference 0.7 percentage points, 95% CI −9.6 to 10.9).

reports.label: Primary two-year report
reports.citation: Parekh DJ, Reis IM, Castle EP, et al. "Robot-assisted radical cystectomy versus open radical cystectomy in patients with bladder cancer (RAZOR): an open-label, randomised, phase 3, non-inferiority trial." *Lancet.* 2018;391(10139):2525-2536.

results.measure: Two-year Kaplan–Meier progression-free survival; risk difference in percentage points (robotic minus open)
results.note: Prespecified lower confidence bound had to exceed −15 percentage points; 41/150 versus 42/152 progressed within two years; two-sided comparison P=0.90.
results.locator: Full text, Table 2 and Results, pp 2529–2530

results.measure: Two-year Kaplan–Meier progression-free survival, modified intention-to-treat sensitivity analysis; risk difference in percentage points
results.note: Sensitivity analysis of the primary endpoint among randomized patients who underwent surgery; 43/159 versus 42/153 progressed within two years.
results.locator: Full text, Table 2 and Statistical analysis, p 2529

results.note: Risk difference in percentage points; no prespecified noninferiority test for this endpoint.

harms.label: Any 90-day Clavien–Dindo grade I–V complication
harms.note: Per-protocol population; difference −1.8 percentage points (95% CI −12.3 to 8.8).

harms.label: Major 90-day Clavien–Dindo grade III–V complication
harms.note: Per-protocol population; difference −0.4 percentage points (95% CI −9.0 to 9.8).

delivery.label: Sites and surgeon experience
delivery.value: 15 US centers; each surgeon had performed at least 10 radical cystectomies in the preceding year and was fellowship trained or had a focused bladder-cancer practice.

delivery.label: Diversion and surgical template
delivery.value: All urinary diversions were extracorporeal; diversion type followed patient and surgeon preference; lymphadenectomy extent and chemotherapy followed institutional preference.
delivery.locator: Full text, Procedures, p 2527 and Discussion, p 2535

values.exp: ileal conduit 113/150 (75%); neobladder 36/150 (24%); continent cutaneous reservoir 1/150 (1%)

delivery.label: Procedures received

values.exp: 150/176 assigned patients in per-protocol analysis; 17/176 had no surgery; 9/176 had a different procedure
values.ctl: 152/174 assigned patients in per-protocol analysis; 21/174 had no surgery; 1/174 had robotic surgery

delivery.note: Five robotic-assigned patients converted to open surgery; Figure 1 lists reasons including locally advanced disease, visualization, Trendelenburg intolerance, and a colonic mass.

delivery.label: Pelvic lymphadenectomy boundaries
delivery.value: Standard dissection extended distally to Cooper’s ligament and the node of Cloquet, proximally to the ureter crossing the common iliac vessels, laterally to the genitofemoral nerve, medially to tissue medial to the hypogastric artery, and posteriorly to the floor of the obturator fossa; extended dissection reached the aortic bifurcation.

reports.followUp: Questionnaires at baseline, three months, and six months
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Materials and Methods, p 451

results.measure: Mixed-model between-approach comparison of subscale and composite mean scores at baseline, three months, and six months
results.note: Surgical approach was this report's primary objective; no prespecified success threshold. FACT-VCI analysis included 231/302 (76.5%) patients with baseline and at least one postoperative questionnaire; arm-specific estimated means are not tabulated in the main text.
results.locator: Full text, Materials and Methods and Results, pp 451–452; Figure 1, p 453

results.endpoint: FACT–VCI total score, adjusted surgical-approach coefficient
results.measure: Three-month multivariable linear regression; robotic minus open, score points; 206/302 had a three-month FACT-VCI questionnaire
results.note: At six months, 198/302 had a FACT-VCI questionnaire; the adjusted robotic-minus-open coefficient was 1.27 points (95% CI −4.33 to 6.87; P=0.654). This regression is separate from the longitudinal mixed-model comparison.
results.locator: Full text, Table 2 and Results, pp 452, 455

results.endpoint: SF-8 physical and mental component scores
results.measure: Mixed-model between-approach comparison at baseline, three months, and six months
results.note: SF-8 analysis included 216/302 (71.5%) patients with baseline and at least one postoperative questionnaire. Within the open arm, six-month physical score was 50.4 versus 45.4 at baseline and mental score was 51 versus 46.8 (both P<0.05); these are within-arm changes, not between-arm effects.
results.locator: Full text, Results, pp 452, 455; Figure 3, p 456

results.endpoint: FACT bladder-cystectomy subscale by diversion type
results.measure: Three-month mixed-model comparison; continent minus noncontinent diversion, score points
results.note: Overall, 67/302 received continent and 235/302 noncontinent diversion; time-specific group denominators were not reported. The separate multivariable regression gave a continent coefficient of −5.50 (95% CI −11.47 to 0.48; P=0.071) at three months and 2.37 (95% CI −4.12 to 8.86; P=0.471) at six months.
results.locator: Full text, Table 1 and Results, p 452; Table 2 and Results, p 455

results.endpoint: SF-8 physical component score by diversion type
results.measure: Six-month mixed-model comparison of continent versus noncontinent diversion, score points
results.note: Estimated means were 51.8 with continent and 46.2 with noncontinent diversion; group-specific six-month questionnaire denominators were not reported. Continent-group score increased from 47.2 at baseline to 51.8 at six months (adjusted P=0.043).
results.locator: Full text, Results, pp 455–456; Figure 3, p 456

delivery.label: Quality-of-life questionnaire completion
delivery.value: Of 302 per-protocol patients, baseline plus at least one postoperative questionnaire was available for FACT-VCI in 231/302 (76.5%) and SF-8 in 216/302 (71.5%); at three months, FACT-VCI 206/302 (68%) and SF-8 179/302 (59.3%); at six months, FACT-VCI 198/302 (65.6%) and SF-8 178/302 (58.9%).
